captions.instagram:
How does the heart work?

Your heart is two pumps in one, beating about 100,000 times a day without a single instruction from you. Take a 3D heart apart, watch its valves slam shut on every lub-dub, and follow the spark that starts each beat.

→ Your heart is a fist-sized muscle that beats about 100,000 times a day.
→ Inside it is two pumps: the right sends blue blood to the lungs, the left sends red blood to the body.
→ Each beat the ventricles fill, then squeeze out about 70 mL. Lub-dub is the valves slamming shut.
→ Each beat starts with a spark from the SA node, the heart’s built-in pacemaker.
→ The spark pauses, then sweeps the ventricles from the bottom up: that is the QRS on an ECG.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/heartclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does the heart work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Your heart is two pumps in one, beating about 100,000 times a day without a single instruction from you. Take a 3D heart apart, watch its valves slam shut on every lub-dub, and follow the spark that starts each beat.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/heartclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/heartclear

In this video:
• Two pumps in one. The heart has four chambers.
• Fill, squeeze, lub-dub. In diastole the ventricles relax and fill; in systole they squeeze out about 70 mL each beat.
• A built-in spark. Each beat starts in the SA node, the heart's natural pacemaker in the right atrium.
• Two circuits, one minute. Blood goes from the right heart through the lungs, where it fills with oxygen to about 98%, back to the left heart and out to the body, returning about 75% full at rest.
• 120 over 80. Blood pressure is the peak of each beat (systolic) over the low point between beats (diastolic).
• When things go wrong. Plaque can narrow a coronary artery, and flow through a tube falls with the fourth power of its radius.

Glassbox opens one box a day: an interactive model of how something works, plus the code behind it.
